paragraphs: In Bava Batra 48b, he was a violent man who wanted to hang Pappi and forced him to sell him his field. Rabbah bar Bar Chana signed a declaration of protest [against the coerced sale].[^1][^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson vocalized text of Bava Batra 48b names Tavi suspending Pappi and compelling the sale, and Rabbah bar bar Chana signing the protest. Hyman’s notice says that Tavi wanted to hang Pappi; that wording is retained.

The whole William Davidson Bava Batra 48b paragraph says Tavi suspended Pappi and names Rabbah bar bar Chana signing the protest. Hyman’s wording ‘wanted to hang’ and his account of the forced field sale are retained; no omitted legal discussion is added.
